_: Measured readings from scripts/art/check-asset-matte.mjs. An asset only appears here when the detector reads it at or above 0.5% - 142 of 148 read below that and need no entry. A reading ABOVE the value recorded here fails the build, because a reading that rises is an export that put the white matte back. Every entry below is a case where the detector is eating ARTWORK, and every reason says what was looked at. Do not add an entry without doing that work; see the header of check-asset-matte.mjs.

public/assets/club-buttons/club/club-ide.reason: Artwork, confirmed by picture and by divergence. The icon is a silver temple, and silver IS smooth, neutral and bright - exactly what the detector calls matte. Cleaning a copy slices the left end of the pediment, the left column's outer face and the left end of the plinth clean off. Re-checking the cleaned copy reads 12.0%: it does not converge, which is the signature of the detector eating art rather than removing a matte. Reverted on 2026-09-10 for this reason.

Artwork. This one CONVERGES (2.8% then 0.1%), which is why convergence alone is not the test. The before/after picture shows the head's dark outline broken on the upper right and lower left and the shoulder bevel chewed off the left edge. Same silver-on-transparent problem as its sibling above. Reverted on 2026-09-10.

public/assets/club-buttons/console/spade.reason: Artwork, and the measurement is unambiguous: this is a 1000x8 horizontal TILING rail, and cleaning removes 40 pixels that are 5 complete columns - 5 in every one of the 8 rows. Tiled across a console that is five transparent slits through the rail. The pixels it wants are the light brushed band in the rail, which is smooth and neutral by design.

public/assets/club-buttons/game-cards/pl.reason: Noise, not matte. 23 pixels, mean luminance 20 - nearly black. It is nibbling the dark glow halo around the green dot, not a white ramp. Before and after are indistinguishable.

public/assets/club-buttons/wallets/mobil.reason: Artwork. 3780 pixels of mean luminance 171 - bright silver - and NOT ONE of them within 4px of the image border; they are spread across rows 12-368 and columns 97-1791 of an 1800x380 plate. A baked matte hugs the outside edge by definition. These are the chrome frame's own highlights.

public/assets/club-buttons/wallets/squar.reason: Sits exactly on the floor and under the cleaner's own threshold, so clean-shell-matte.py writes nothing for it. Recorded so the number is pinned rather than left one rounding tick away from failing the build.

public/assets/diamond-spins/wheel-matte-.reason: Matte gunmetal frame and its antialiased silhouette, inspected at full size on black on 2026-09-19. The detector removes 13487 edge pixels with mean RGB luminance 104.94; none exceeds 200 and only 831 are fully opaque. The removed band follows the horizontal steel rim and corner housing shadows, not a white export background. An in-memory cleaned copy converges to 0.0%, but convergence alone is insufficient: it removes the frame silhouette shading. Keep the approved matte frame and pin this exact reading.

public/assets/diamond-spins/wheel-select.reason: Artwork, the known silver-at-the-border case, inspected at full size on black on 2026-09-21. This is the centre holder cut from the approved wheel-selector-mount-v1.png around its hub axis (owner ruling 2026-09-21, R5: only the holder and the pointer, no side arcs), with the two cuts feathered over 36 px so the arm ends softly. The detector removes 9575 pixels of mean RGB luminance 134.8, only 32 of them fully opaque and only 673 above 200, all in columns 3-105 and 415-517 of the 520-wide crop: the two feathered brushed-steel arm stubs, which are smooth, neutral and bright by design and sit at the image border because that is where the cut is. The hub, clamps and everything above and below them read clean. A cleaned copy loses the arm stubs entirely, which is the art, not a matte. Pin the reading.
